title: Where Does Weak-to-Strong Generalization Break by Task Type?

original_idea.body:
# Where Does Weak-to-Strong Generalization Break by Task Type?

**Problem:** The dependence of W2S on task structure (subjective vs verifiable vs adversarial) is under-mapped.

**Direction:** Using the open W2S code, run weak-supervises-strong with small open models across a diverse task set (verifiable, subjective, adversarial). Measure performance-gap-recovered per task type and whether the confidence-based auxiliary loss helps unevenly.

**Why it matters:** Knowing which task types W2S fails on tells us where weak human oversight of strong models is least trustworthy.

**Relevant context:** Burns et al. (OpenAI 2023); arXiv:2403.09472.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: mapping where W2S fails by task type directly informs where weak oversight is least trustworthy.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Uses released W2S code with small models, but multi-task fine-tuning is guided rather than trivial.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused PGR-by-task-type study; three task setups add some dependency.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: W2S-when-it-fails is external-friendly with public code/models; some lab attention but mostly classification.

low_compute.reasoning: W2S fine-tuning of small models across tasks is single mid-GPU-days.

novelty.reasoning: W2S exists; the task-type-dependence mapping may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: W2S studied on classification; task-type breakdown plausibly open.
